description: Only panel (b) of Fig. 8 is supplied (the "(b)" label sits in the upper-left corner); panel (a), which the caption says plots mean grain size and dislocation density, is absent from the image. Panel (b) is a dual-y-axis line plot whose two y-axes are both broken by a slash mark. The x-axis is "Hot-rolling reduction (%)" running 40-90, with three data points near 45, 68 and 85% (the samples HR45, HR68, HR82). The left y-axis is "Volume fraction (%)" with an upper segment 3.2-4.8 and a lower segment 0.0-0.4; the right y-axis is "mean particle size (nm)" with an upper segment 200-360 and a lower segment ticked 0.5 and 1.0. Four error-barred series appear: "Volume fraction of (Nb,Mo,W)C" (open squares, lower-left segment, flat near the middle of the 0.0-0.4 segment), "Volume fraction κ-carbide" (open circles, upper-left segment, falling from between the 3.2 and 3.6 gridlines at HR45 to just above 3.2 at HR68, then rising to just below 4.0 at HR82), "Mean size of (Nb,Mo,W)C" (red open squares, upper-right segment, nearly constant between the 240 and 280 nm gridlines) and "Mean size of κ-carbide" (red open circles, lower-right segment, nearly flat). The figure demonstrates that particle sizes stay essentially constant across rolling reductions while the κ-carbide volume fraction dips at intermediate reduction.

subfigures.description: Broken-axis dual-y-axis line plot: x = Hot-rolling reduction (%) 40-90 (three points near 45, 68, 85); left y = Volume fraction (%) broken into 3.2-4.8 and 0.0-0.4; right y = mean particle size (nm) broken into 200-360 and a lower segment ticked 0.5 and 1.0. Legend: grey open squares = Volume fraction of (Nb,Mo,W)C, grey open circles = Volume fraction κ-carbide, red open squares = Mean size of (Nb,Mo,W)C, red open circles = Mean size of κ-carbide. All series have error bars. The κ-carbide volume fraction shows a minimum at the intermediate (HR68) reduction; the other three series are near-flat.

observations.observation: The supplied image contains only panel (b) of Fig. 8 — the label "(b)" is printed in the upper-left corner — and panel (a) is not visible.
The x-axis is labelled "Hot-rolling reduction (%)" and spans 40 to 90, with data points at three reductions near 45, 68 and 85%.
The left y-axis is labelled "Volume fraction (%)" and is broken: upper segment spans 3.2 to 4.8, lower segment spans 0.0 to 0.4.
The right y-axis is labelled "mean particle size (nm)" and is broken: upper segment spans 200 to 360, lower segment is ticked 0.5 and 1.0.
The legend contains four entries exactly as printed: "Volume fraction of (Nb,Mo,W)C", "Volume fraction κ-carbide", "Mean size of (Nb,Mo,W)C" and "Mean size of κ-carbide".

The κ-carbide volume-fraction series (open circles, upper-left segment) falls from between the 3.2 and 3.6 gridlines at HR45 to just above the 3.2 gridline at the intermediate reduction, then rises to just below the 4.0 gridline at the largest reduction.
The (Nb,Mo,W)C volume-fraction series (open squares, lower-left segment) is nearly flat, lying within the 0.0-0.4 segment.
The (Nb,Mo,W)C mean particle-size series (red open squares, upper-right segment) stays essentially constant between the 240 and 280 nm gridlines at all three rolling reductions.
The κ-carbide mean particle-size series (red open circles, lower-right segment) is nearly flat across the three reductions.
Every plotted series carries vertical error bars.
The caption states that Fig. 8(a) shows the variation of mean grain size, excluding and including twin boundaries, and the dislocation density of the samples at different hot-rolling reductions.
The caption states that Fig. 8(b) shows the volume fractions and mean particle sizes of the κ-carbides and (Nb,Mo,W)C particles of the three investigated samples.
The citing text states the three investigated samples are HR45, HR68 and HR82, corresponding to hot-rolling reductions of 45%, 68% and 82%.

The citing text states that because of the large size and low volume fraction of the micron-sized (Nb,Mo,W)C particles their Orowan-bypassing strengthening contribution was negligible, whereas κ-carbide shearing contributions were 60.16, 58.04 and 60.98 MPa for HR45, HR68 and HR82, and submicron (Nb,Mo,W)C contributions were 6.39, 6.65 and 6.52 MPa; it concludes that precipitate strengthening did not contribute to the strength increment with larger rolling reduction.

The citing text states GND densities obtained from KAM maps were 2.71×10^13, 7.49×10^13 and 9.87×10^13 m^-2 and the resulting dislocation strengthening 56.29, 93.67 and 107.50 MPa for HR45, HR68 and HR82; these values belong to Fig. 8(a), which is not included in the supplied image.
